source_evidence: Exempt reporting advisers are investment advisers that are not required to register with the SEC but are subject to certain SEC reporting, recordkeeping, and other obligations.
answer: An exempt reporting adviser (ERA) is not required to register with the SEC, but still has certain SEC reporting, recordkeeping, and other obligations. An ERA may advise private funds only; it cannot provide investment advice directly to individuals. ERAs are subject to the same prohibitions against fraud as registered advisers, and state requirements can vary.
